reserve ratio reflects fair value of collateral and cannot be moved cheaply within or between transactions
changed_by: direct token transfers to the pair followed by sync

dependencies.assumption: reserves are updated before any external call so input is counted once

findings.title: Unprotected LendingPool.setPair lets any caller replace the price source
findings.mechanism: setPair lacks the onlyOwner modifier that setOwner has. Any address can point `pair` at a contract whose getReserves returns arbitrary values. price() trusts it without checking token0/token1 identity, so the LTV checks in borrow and withdrawCollateral are evaluated against a caller-chosen price.
preconditions: Caller has any non-zero collateral deposited (or none, for withdrawCollateral of others is not possible; borrow needs collateralOf>0)
findings.impact: Entire debtToken balance of the pool can be borrowed against negligible collateral, and collateral can be withdrawn while debt remains; total loss of lender funds / insolvency.
findings.how_to_validate: From a non-owner address call setPair(mock) and assert it reverts with "owner"; currently it succeeds. Additionally assert that after setPair to a mock with r1/r0 inflated, borrow(debtToken.balanceOf(pool)) by a user with 1 wei collateral does not succeed (it currently does).

findings.title: Spot AMM reserves used as lending oracle are manipulable via donation+sync and swaps
findings.mechanism: price() reads instantaneous reserves r1/r0. SimplePair.sync is public and sets reserves to raw balances, so transferring token1 to the pair and calling sync raises the collateral price in the same transaction; no TWAP, no deviation bound, no minimum liquidity. borrow/withdrawCollateral then evaluate LTV at the inflated price. With no liquidation function, resulting bad debt is never cleared.
preconditions: Pair liquidity is shallow relative to pool debtToken liquidity
Manipulator has (or can borrow within a transaction) token1 to move the ratio
findings.impact: Borrowing beyond the fair value of collateral, leaving undercollateralised debt the protocol cannot recover; lender/protocol insolvency up to the debtToken held by LendingPool, net of manipulation cost.
findings.how_to_validate: In a unit test with a seeded pair, record price(); transfer X token1 to the pair and call sync(); assert price() is unchanged or bounded (it currently scales by (r1+X)/r1). Then assert that a position opened at the manipulated price has debt*10000 <= collateral*fairPrice*7500 after the reserves are restored (currently violated).

findings.title: ShareVault.withdraw rounds shares burned down, allowing withdrawal of assets for zero or too few shares
findings.mechanism: shares = assets*totalSupply/totalAssets floors. Whenever totalAssets > totalSupply (share price > 1, which anyone can cause by transferring asset directly to the vault since totalAssets is balanceOf), withdraw(assets) with assets*totalSupply < totalAssets burns 0 shares yet transfers `assets`. Repetition, or a single call at a high share price, extracts assets belonging to other holders. There is no require(shares>0) and no round-up.
preconditions: totalAssets() > totalSupply (e.g. after a direct donation or accrued gains)
Caller holds at least 0 shares (balanceOf -= 0 does not underflow)
findings.impact: Theft of other depositors' underlying; vault becomes insolvent relative to outstanding shares.
findings.how_to_validate: Set up supply=1 share, totalAssets=1e18 (deposit 1 then donate). From an address with 0 shares call withdraw(1e18-1); assert it reverts or burns >=1 share. Invariant assertion: after any withdraw, totalAssets()*1e18/totalSupply (price per share) is non-decreasing for remaining holders.

findings.title: ShareVault first-depositor share inflation via donation to balance-based totalAssets
findings.mechanism: totalAssets depends on asset.balanceOf, changeable by any direct transfer. With a tiny totalSupply, a donation makes assets*supply/totalAssets floor to 0 (or a heavily rounded number) for a subsequent depositor; deposit does not reject 0 shares, so the depositor's assets accrue to existing holders, who redeem them.
preconditions: Vault empty or with very small totalSupply
A later deposit smaller than (or not a multiple of) the inflated price per share
findings.impact: Loss of depositor funds to the early shareholder.
findings.how_to_validate: Deposit 1 wei from A, donate D to the vault, then deposit d<D+1 from B; assert B's shares > 0 and redeem by B returns approximately d (currently B gets 0 shares and A's redeem returns ~D+d+1).

findings.title: RewardPool.stake does not checkpoint the user, so new or added stake earns retroactive rewards
findings.mechanism: stake calls _updatePool only; userRewardPerTokenPaid[msg.sender] stays at its old value (0 for a new staker). earned() then multiplies the full new balance by rewardPerToken minus the stale checkpoint, crediting rewards accrued before the stake existed. A two-step path (stake, then claim in the same block) pays out the accumulated rewardPerToken on the whole stake; existing stakers adding stake are similarly over-credited.
preconditions: rewardPerTokenStored > 0 (pool has been running with stakers)
findings.impact: Reward token balance drained by late stakers; honest stakers' claims fail for lack of funds (insolvency of reward accounting). If rewardToken == stakeToken, staked principal is drained too.
findings.how_to_validate: Let A stake and advance time T; then B stakes S and, without advancing time, call earned(B); assert earned(B) == 0 (currently S*rewardPerToken/1e18). Invariant: sum of earned over all users <= rewardRate * elapsed time while staked.

findings.title: SimplePair.swap0For1 performs the token1 transfer before updating reserves (reentrancy with hook tokens)
findings.mechanism: in0 is computed as balance minus cached reserve0 and the k-check uses cached reserves; token1.transfer runs before sync(). If token1 invokes a recipient hook, a re-entrant swap0For1 sees the same in0 and the same (not yet reduced) reserve1 and passes the k-check again, so one input is credited twice. Also, since LendingPool reads reserves via getReserves, a reentrant reader during the callback sees stale reserves.
preconditions: token1 has transfer callbacks to `to` (ERC777-style); not true for a plain ERC20
findings.impact: Drain of pair token1 reserves and corresponding oracle distortion for LendingPool.
findings.how_to_validate: With a mock token1 that calls back into swap0For1 from the recipient, assert the second nested call reverts (or that total token1 out <= amount allowed by k for the single input). Fix check: a nonReentrant lock or sync before transfer makes the assertion hold.

findings.title: Lending positions have no liquidation path, so any price move or manipulation leaves permanent bad debt
findings.mechanism: LTV is only enforced at borrow/withdraw time. When collateral price falls (organically or via swap0For1 which pushes r1/r0 down), nothing permits a third party to repay and seize collateral; the borrower has no incentive to repay debt exceeding collateral value.
preconditions: Collateral price declines after borrowing (or manipulated borrow as in the oracle finding)
findings.impact: Protocol insolvency: outstanding debt exceeds collateral value with no recovery mechanism.
findings.how_to_validate: After borrowing at max LTV, move price down 50% via swap0For1 + sync; assert there exists a callable function by a third party that reduces debtOf(borrower) and transfers collateral (none exists).

notes: Dependencies traced: LendingPool->SimplePair (pair pointer + spot reserves), all contracts->token balanceOf/transfer behaviour. Lower-severity observations not raised as findings: (1) LendingPool.price divides by r0, so before the pair is first synced (r0==0) borrow and withdrawCollateral revert, locking collateral even for zero-debt users (liveness; also the case after setPair to an empty pair). (2) SimplePair.sync truncates balances to uint112; only reachable with very large token supplies but would distort price. (3) Neither the LendingPool constructor nor setPair checks pair.token0()==collateral and pair.token1()==debtToken; a misordered pair inverts the price. (4) PayoutSplitter.distribute reverts entirely if any single recipient transfer fails (blacklist/pausable token), locking all funds (liveness); dust from flooring is carried to the next distribution, not lost. (5) ShareVault.deposit credits shares on the nominal amount, so a fee-on-transfer asset over-mints shares; withdraw/redeem divide by totalAssets/totalSupply and revert when either is zero. (6) RewardPool.setRewardRate does not check the pool is funded; unbacked rates make later claimers insolvent (owner-trust issue). (7) LendingPool.borrowers grows unbounded; borrowerCount is a view, so only off-chain impact. PayoutSplitter.owner and the unused RewardPool owner beyond setRewardRate have no further effect.
